items.title: Create a runtime artifact registry
items.context: Define runtime/log/cache artifact paths and gitignore patterns in a single core registry instead of scattered string checks.
items.userSees: `koala doctor` prints `Runtime artifacts: no tracked runtime artifacts found` on a clean repo, and registry tests list `.koala/activity.jsonl` as `materialHash: exclude`.

happy.desc: The runtime artifact registry exports explicit entries for current and legacy Koala runtime logs/cache paths, including their ignore patterns and repair behavior.

edge.desc: The registry does not classify .koala/story artifacts, source files, requirements docs, package manifests, or koala.config.json as runtime artifacts.

adversarial.desc: A future consumer cannot satisfy tests by hardcoding only .koala/activity.jsonl while omitting legacy activity and runtime/cache paths from the registry.

verificationEvidence.note: verification freshness smoke asserts the runtime registry exports current and legacy activity paths as non-material metadata
verification freshness smoke keeps source, package, config, fixture, and requirements files material while excluding only registry runtime artifacts
smoke covers both .koala/activity.jsonl and docs/story/activity.jsonl so consumers cannot satisfy coverage by hardcoding only one runtime path

items.title: Wire freshness and dirty-risk checks to the registry
items.context: currentMaterialHash and changed-file freshness must exclude runtime artifacts; baseline risk and DONE-related hints should classify tracked runtime logs as repairable runtime artifacts.
items.userSees: `npm run test:verification-freshness` prints `✓ verification freshness smoke passed`, including tracked `.koala/activity.jsonl` staying `covered` while source/config changes stay `stale`.

happy.desc: currentMaterialHash and checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit ignore runtime artifacts from the registry, so tracked .koala/activity.jsonl changes keep evidence covered.
baseline risk uses the registry to classify runtime artifacts as volatile instead of material dirty paths.

edge.desc: Material files such as packages/main/src/core/verification.ts, package-lock.json, koala.config.json, and docs/requirements remain material and still stale evidence when changed.

adversarial.desc: A tracked legacy docs/story/activity.jsonl change is also ignored for material freshness, preventing old storage migrations from reintroducing the stale loop.

verificationEvidence.note: materialHash-backed freshness stays covered when tracked .koala/activity.jsonl changes because currentMaterialHash excludes registry runtime artifacts
baseline-risk smoke hides .omx runtime residue while still surfacing material user edits before INIT_CHECK
real source, package, config, fixture, and requirements files still stale evidence after material changes
tracked legacy docs/story/activity.jsonl also remains metadata-only for freshness and coverage reporting

items.title: Make init and doctor repair runtime artifact drift
items.context: koala init should merge required ignore patterns into existing .gitignore; doctor should detect tracked runtime artifacts and provide repair guidance or repair path.
items.userSees: In an existing project, `koala init --profile=core /tmp/app` prints `✓ .gitignore (merged koala runtime ignores)`, and `koala doctor` prints `Runtime artifacts: tracked .koala/activity.jsonl -> git rm --cached .koala/activity.jsonl`.

happy.desc: koala init merges missing runtime artifact ignore patterns into an existing .gitignore while preserving existing user content.
koala doctor reports tracked runtime artifacts with a concrete git rm --cached repair hint.

edge.desc: If all required ignore patterns are already present, koala init leaves .gitignore unchanged except for normal init output.

adversarial.desc: doctor does not mutate git tracking without --repair, and doctor --repair only untracks registered runtime artifacts rather than broad .koala/story evidence.

verificationEvidence.note: entrypoints verification covers merging missing runtime ignore lines into an existing .gitignore under a managed block
validation protocol smoke makes doctor report tracked .koala/activity.jsonl with a concrete git rm --cached repair command
entrypoints verification keeps an existing .gitignore byte-for-byte unchanged when all required runtime ignores are already present
doctor --repair untracks only registry-approved runtime artifacts and leaves .koala/story evidence tracked

items.title: Add hard-coded regression coverage
items.context: Update freshness smoke and add contract coverage so .koala/activity.jsonl is runtime metadata, not material, and required ignore patterns cannot drift.
items.userSees: `npm run test:entrypoints` prints `entrypoints verified`, and `npm run test:verification-freshness` prints `✓ verification freshness smoke passed` after the tracked-runtime-artifact regression case runs.

happy.desc: npm run test:verification-freshness passes and explicitly proves runtime artifacts do not stale materialHash-backed evidence.
npm run test:entrypoints passes and covers init .gitignore merge behavior for existing projects.

edge.desc: The freshness smoke still proves real material paths are stale, so the runtime exclusion is not overly broad.

adversarial.desc: A tracked runtime artifact scenario is tested, not just an ignored untracked file scenario.

verificationEvidence.note: verification freshness smoke proves runtime artifacts do not stale materialHash-backed evidence even when the runtime file is tracked
entrypoints verification covers existing-project .gitignore merge and no-churn behavior
the smoke still marks source, package, config, fixture, and requirements paths stale so the exclusion stays narrow
tracked runtime artifact coverage is explicit in the smoke, not just an ignored-untracked-file scenario
